statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable API is the containerd CRI server CreateContainer checkpoint-restore path. Trivy scans a local image archive through NewArchiveImage; Code Polishy never runs a containerd server, restores a checkpoint, or mounts a runtime socket into the scanner.

Offline archive scans have no network and do not create gRPC or containerd clients. The sole networked operation downloads the database using Trivy pkg/remote and pkg/x/http with the standard net/http transport, not golang.org/x/net/http2; the scanner image also disables the standard HTTP/2 client with GODEBUG=http2client=0.

The affected gRPC HTTP/2 transport requires a live client or server connection. Archive scans use the standalone local service with no runtime socket or network, and database download uses the standard net/http registry client. Neither operation starts a gRPC transport.

The vulnerable operation is xDS server routing of an HTTP/2 request without authority or Host. Code Polishy invokes only version, database download, and standalone offline image-archive scans; it never starts a gRPC or xDS server.

The affected net/http file-serving handlers parse attacker-controlled Range request headers. The scanner starts no HTTP server and uses no file-serving transport; its only networked operation is an outgoing HTTPS database download.

The minimal scanner image sets GODEBUG=http2client=0. Trivy clones the standard net/http transport for database downloads, so Go does not negotiate HTTP/2 or process HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames. Archive scans run with --network none and no server mode is enabled.

The affected crypto/tls decodeInnerClientHello operation processes ECH ClientHello extensions on a TLS server. Code Polishy never starts a TLS server in the scanner: database download is an HTTPS client, and archive scans run without network access.
